subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Paper 2 of the Edexcel International GCSE Art and Design, what does the abbreviation 'ESA' stand for?
questions.explain: Paper 2 is the Externally Set Assignment, based on a theme provided by the exam board.

questions.q: Who sets the theme and starting points for the Externally Set Assignment?
questions.explain: The theme is 'externally set', meaning it is issued by Pearson Edexcel rather than chosen by the teacher or student.

questions.q: What proportion of the total qualification does Paper 2 (the ESA) contribute?
questions.explain: Paper 1 (coursework) and Paper 2 (the ESA) each carry 50% of the overall marks.

questions.q: The Externally Set Assignment is made up of which two main phases?
options: A preparatory study period followed by supervised time to produce the final outcome
A written exam followed by an oral presentation
A group project followed by an individual essay
A mock exam followed by a resit
questions.explain: Students first develop preparatory studies and then create the final piece under supervised conditions.

questions.q: During which phase of the ESA must the work be completed unaided under supervised conditions?
questions.explain: The final outcome must be produced as the student's own unaided work during the supervised period.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the preparatory studies in the ESA?
options: To research, generate and develop ideas in response to the theme before the final outcome
To write a formal essay evaluating famous artists
To copy the exam board's example images exactly
To rehearse a timed drawing with no development
questions.explain: Preparatory studies allow students to investigate sources, experiment and refine ideas ahead of the supervised piece.

questions.q: May a student bring their completed preparatory studies into the supervised session?
options: Yes, preparatory work is taken in and used as the basis for the final outcome
No, all preparatory work must be left outside
Only if the teacher completes it for them
Only the exam board's images may be used
questions.explain: Students use their own preparatory studies to inform and produce the final outcome under supervision.

questions.q: How many assessment objectives are used to assess the Edexcel International GCSE Art and Design ESA?
questions.explain: Both papers are assessed against the same four assessment objectives, AO1 to AO4.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on developing ideas through investigations and critical understanding of sources?
questions.explain: AO1 covers developing ideas through investigation, demonstrating critical understanding of sources.

questions.q: Which assessment objective concerns refining work by experimenting with appropriate media, materials, techniques and processes?
questions.explain: AO2 is about refining ideas by selecting and experimenting with appropriate media and techniques.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is about recording ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses?
questions.explain: AO3 covers recording ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is most directly demonstrated by a resolved final outcome that realises the student's intentions?
questions.explain: AO4 concerns presenting a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions and shows understanding of visual language.

questions.q: What does the externally set theme provide to the candidate?
options: Starting points and stimuli from which a personal response is developed
A finished composition to reproduce exactly
A single compulsory medium that must be used
questions.explain: The theme offers stimuli, and each candidate develops their own individual, personal response.

questions.q: A student studying the theme 'Structures' looks at an artist's work, annotates it and produces media experiments inspired by it. Which is the best use of this artist reference?
options: Using it as a springboard to develop and inform their own personal ideas
Tracing and submitting the artist's image as the final outcome
Ignoring it because only the student's own drawings count
Copying the artist's finished piece without any development
questions.explain: Artist references should inform and inspire the student's own developing personal response, not be reproduced.

questions.q: During the preparatory period a student trials watercolour, collage and printmaking to see which best suits their idea. This activity most clearly evidences which assessment objective?
options: AO2 (refining and experimenting with media and techniques)
questions.explain: Experimenting with and selecting appropriate media to refine ideas is the focus of AO2.

questions.q: In the supervised session, what should the final outcome demonstrate?
options: The realisation of the intentions developed through the preparatory studies
A completely new idea unrelated to any preparatory work
Work finished with direct help from the teacher
An exact copy of another artist's painting
questions.explain: The final outcome should bring the candidate's developed intentions to a resolved conclusion.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT permitted during the supervised production of the final outcome?
options: Receiving direct assistance so that the work is no longer the student's own
Using media the student practised earlier
questions.explain: The supervised final outcome must be the candidate's own unaided work.

questions.q: Which of these best shows a candidate genuinely 'responding to a set theme'?
options: Interpreting the theme personally and developing individual ideas from it
Selecting a different subject that ignores the theme
Reproducing the exam paper's example image
questions.explain: Responding to the theme means interpreting it and developing a genuine personal response.

questions.q: Good preparatory studies for the ESA should primarily show what?
options: A clear journey of investigation, development and refinement toward the intended outcome
A single unrelated finished drawing with no development
Only written notes with no visual work
An exact replica of a classmate's project
questions.explain: Effective preparatory work evidences the progression of ideas from research through to a planned outcome.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Art and Design specifications; Paper 2: Externally Set Assignment
